messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for api.redwood.ai (us-east-1). error-rate: 12% over 3m, request volume spike on /v1/generate. Paging oncall.
Maya (eng-runtime): acked. I'm pulling traces and the gateway logs now. seeing a bunch of upstream 429s bubbling as 502/504 at the edge.
Maya (eng-runtime): metrics: 5xx rate by code: 502 ~7%, 504 ~3%, 500 ~2%. top upstream response is 429 from quota-service.
Ben (eng-sre): on my way. can we confirm recent quota config deploy around 17:55? that's when volume increased.
Victor (eng-infra): there was a config push to quota-configmap at ~17:50 from CI: commit abcdef4.
Dave (support): getting P0 customer D reports timeouts and errors for embeddings calls. CRO is asking for ETA.
Carla (product): putting a short note to CS: "We're investigating increased errors; engineering oncall is mitigating." keep me updated for customer comms.
Maya (eng-runtime): quick diagnostic: logs from gateway show lines like:
```
2026-03-15T17:58:12.345Z gateway-1 ERROR upstream response 429 quota exceeded user=acct:12345 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T17:58:12.678Z gateway-1 WARN converting upstream 429 -> 502
```
Looks like quota-service started rejecting tokens.
Ben (eng-sre): can we toggle quota enforcement to permissive for traffic while we debug? I want to avoid circuiting user traffic.
Victor (eng-infra): we have a runtime flag we can flip per-region: `QUOTA_ENFORCE=true` in the runtime-config configmap. I can patch it to false for us-east-1.
Ben (eng-sre): do it. Post the exact command so I can watch metrics.
Victor (eng-infra): executing now: `kubectl -n infra patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"QUOTA_ENFORCE":"false"}}'` (rolling restart not required for gateway; it reads config periodically).
PagerDuty: Ben (eng-sre) acknowledged the page (oncall).
Maya (eng-runtime): flipping flag yielded immediate drop in 502/504 at the edge. 5xx fell from 12% -> 2.8% within 90s. Some customers still see 429s from quota-service directly (bypassed for gateway path) but overall user-facing errors much lower.
Dave (support): passing update to customer D: "We've identified quota enforcement as root cause; we've temporarily relaxed enforcement while engineering investigates. Expect service to recover; will update in 30m."
Carla (product): good. any risk to abuse while enforcement relaxed?
Ben (eng-sre): short-term risk is increased cost/abuse. we've limited to us-east-1 only and monitoring. we'll keep strict observability on spikes and can re-enable at any time.
Maya (eng-runtime): digging into quota-service: looks like a misapplied rule in the configmap `quota-policies` — a new rule had a missing denominator which effectively set limits extremely low for token-based quotas. sample snippet from config:
```
- name: per_api_key_token_limit
  type: token
  limit: "0"
  window_seconds: 60
```
That `limit: "0"` looks suspicious and matches the timelines.
Victor (eng-infra): that was introduced by PR #4127 (author: infra-ci) rolled at 17:49.
Ben (eng-sre): action plan: 1) patch quota-policies to sane defaults (rollback PR), 2) keep QUOTA_ENFORCE=false until patch propagated and we validate, 3) postmortem & revert gating.
Maya (eng-runtime): rolling patch to restore previous quota policy: `kubectl apply -f /deploy/configs/quota-policies-backup.yaml` — patch started.
Ben (eng-sre): I'm watching the metrics. once the quota-service starts returning 200s for health checks and upstream 429s drop, we'll flip QUOTA_ENFORCE back on and observe.
Victor (eng-infra): quota-service logs now show policy reload: "loaded 18 policies" and earlier errors about denominator parsing are gone.
Maya (eng-runtime): edge 5xx down to 1.1% over 3m. upstream 429s decreased by 95% in the same window.
Dave (support): sending updated customer note: "Errors significantly reduced; temporary mitigation applied; engineering reverting a misconfigured quota rule. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
Carla (product): coordinate with legal/CS for customers on reserved capacity; some enterprise customers saw increased latency and may request credits.
Ben (eng-sre): re-enabling enforcement in 2m to validate safe on-path behavior. will watch for regressions.
Maya (eng-runtime): re-enabled: patched QUOTA_ENFORCE=true for us-east-1. repeating canaries show baseline error rates.
PagerDuty: Tom (oncall-night) scheduled to take handoff at 20:00 UTC.
Ben (eng-sre): handoff note -> Tom: system stable, root cause a bad quota config introduced by PR #4127. temporary enforcement disabled for us-east-1 while we fixed policy. Trend graphs + logs are in the incident runbook channel.
Tom (oncall-night): ack. I'll monitor for 2h and run the quota policy smoke test: `python infra/tools/quota_smoke.py --region us-east-1 --sample-keys 20` every 15m.
Carla (product): please prepare a short customer-facing timeline for tomorrow: include detection time, mitigation steps (enforcement relax + config rollback), impact window, and mitigation status.
Ben (eng-sre): Post-incident next steps (unassigned/outstanding):
- Create postmortem and link PR #4127 review (owner: infra-ci).
- Add CI gate: validate quota config schema to catch `limit: "0"` or missing denominators (owner: eng-infra).
- Add automated canary for quota-service rolling changes (owner: eng-runtime).
- Review customer impact & credits (owner: support/product).
Maya (eng-runtime): temporary mitigation removed; full production validation looks good. marking incident as 'mitigated' but keeping thread open for follow-ups.
Ben (eng-sre): closing timeline note: first alert 1998765432, mitigation (flag flip) 1998765480, config rollback 1998765560, re-enable enforcement 1998765840. final reduction validated 1998765920.
IncidentBot: Incident marked mitigated. Please file postmortem within 72h.
Tom (oncall-night): taking handoff.
Dave (support): closing customer alert with status: resolved -> will follow up tomorrow with timeline.
Carla (product): thanks team. we'll reconvene for the postmortem write-up and customer comms.
